records.name: Northeast Philadelphia Community Kollel
records.summary: A Torah study center in Rhawnhurst that offers classes, a weekly newsletter of Torah insights, and study sessions. Its Wednesday evening class on Jewish law is live on Zoom, with a join link on the site.
records.what_you_do: Join the Wednesday Zoom class, read the weekly newsletter, or watch recorded talks on the site. Two other listed programs are for teen boys and for businessmen, and the site gives no times or costs for most programs.

schedule.text: A live class on Halacha (Jewish law) every Wednesday at 8:30 on Zoom. The site also lists a Tuesday night program for teen boys held at the Kollel.

cost.text: No fee is listed for the Wednesday class. The site asks for donations on its Support Us page.

first_step.how: Use the join link on the shiur page for the Wednesday 8:30 Zoom class, or email info@northeastkollel.org with questions first.
first_step.basis: The Wednesday class has a direct Zoom join link, and the site says it welcomes Jews of any education or observance. It does not say whether beginners get their own class.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Wednesday class is a live Halacha (Jewish law) session on Zoom at 8:30. The site does not say how long it runs, who usually attends, or what the format looks like.
first_visit_tips: Install Zoom before 8:30 so the join link works the first time.
Email info@northeastkollel.org before you come to ask whether the class suits someone new to the material.

records.notes: The Wednesday class page gives no street address and no eligibility rules. Newsletter notices dated 09/15/2026 say minyanim resume at the Kollel, but no minyan times are published, so none are listed. The recorded talks link carried over from tier 1 was not opened in this pass. The events calendar showed no listed events.

records.name: Community Made
records.summary: Neighbors in East Oak Lane who connect residents, local businesses, and groups to help the area live and work well together. Volunteers and youth prepare and deliver meals to older neighbors each week, and the group runs weekly wellness check-ins.
records.what_you_do: Help prepare and deliver meals to older neighbors, do wellness check-ins, stock and check the community fridges, or help at porch conversations, pop-up events, and festivals.

schedule.text: Volunteers prepare and deliver meals to older neighbors each week, and the team runs weekly wellness check-ins. Porch conversations, pop-up events, and seasonal festivals are posted on the site when they are scheduled.

cost.text: The volunteer page lists no fee. The site also takes donations and lists a membership option it calls a support plan.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the volunteer page, or email Hello@CommunityMadePhilly.org, and ask about the Neighbor Companion role (meal delivery and check-ins).
first_step.basis: The volunteer page has a contact form and an email address, and the FAQ says anyone can get involved by sending a message. The site does not describe what a first shift looks like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a first shift runs or who you would work with. The listed roles include delivering meals and doing check-ins with homebound older neighbors, helping at festivals, and stocking and checking community fridges.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come to ask which role suits a first-timer.
Watch the event list for porch conversations and festivals, which are a way to meet the team in person.

records.notes: The event list says there are no events at the moment. The newest dated post is from August 2025, so status rests on that plus the working site. The volunteer page gives no shift length, schedule, or requirements for most roles. The Friends of Ellwood role supports a school in the area; the school side was not checked.

records.name: Confident Queen Collective
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit with live and online programs for teen girls in leadership, mental wellness, and life skills. Mentors, advisors, and coaches run the programs, and the group has a parent support team.
records.what_you_do: Teen girls can take part in the live or online leadership and wellness programs. The site does not say how to sign up, so ask by email or phone.

cost.text: Program fees are not shown on the site. Donations are the only money request shown.

first_step.how: Email info@confidentqueen.org or call 267-482-0330 and ask how a teen or parent can join a program. You can also sign up for monthly updates on the homepage.
first_step.basis: The site shows no program page, fees, or sign-up steps, and it asks visitors to contact the group directly.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site says the programs are live and digital and are run by mentors, advisors, and coaches. It does not describe a session, how long one lasts, or what a teen does in one.
first_visit_tips: Ask which live session is next and whether it is for teens, parents, or both.
Ask about fees before you sign up, since the site does not show them.

records.notes: Verdict left at publish, but please review: the site still lists live and digital programs and a working contact, yet the newest of 18 dated blog posts is from February 15, 2024 (more than 24 months old), so status is dormant. The /programs and /events pages return 404, and the About page has no program details. One web search found no sign-up route; a 2022 news article it surfaced was not opened and is not used. Tier 1 said many programs run through schools; the homepage read this pass does not say that, so the claim was removed.

records.name: Congregation Ahavas Torah
records.summary: A shul in Northeast Philadelphia with about 100 member families. It holds daily prayer services and regular Torah classes (shiurim) led by its rav.
records.what_you_do: Attend daily prayer services or a Torah class, ask one of the listed hosts to arrange a Shabbos stay with meals, or check the membership page for dues and seating.

schedule.text: Daily minyanim, with times on an external davening schedule linked from the site. Evening Torah classes run most nights, including Daf Yomi on Sunday to Wednesday at 8:15 pm and Thursday at 7:15 pm. Some classes are for women only, and the site says class times may change.

cost.text: Dues listed on the renewal page: $900 for a family, $450 for a single member, $250 for an associate, and $0 for a first-year member. The site does not say whether visitors pay to attend services.

first_step.how: Contact one of the Shabbos hospitality hosts listed on the Shabbos Hospitality page to arrange a place to stay and meals for Shabbos.
first_step.basis: The Shabbos hospitality page says visitors are welcome and names who to contact to arrange a stay and meals. It does not describe what a visitor should expect at services or classes.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site says visitors are hosted for Shabbos or other times, with a place to stay and meals arranged by a host. It does not describe sleeping arrangements, how long a stay lasts, or what it costs, so ask your host.
first_visit_tips: Check the daily minyan times on the external davening schedule, since the site does not print them.
Confirm class times before you go, because the site says they may change.

records.notes: The Shabbos hospitality page names three host contacts. Their personal names and contact details are left out of this record. The membership page is a renewal page and does not describe joining as a new member. The contact page lists a phone number with no label and no general office email, so neither is added. Women's classes meet at 8032 Dorcas Street per the shiur schedule. No dated items were found, so status stays probably_active.

records.name: Congregation B'nai Israel Ohev Zedek
records.summary: A Northeast Philadelphia synagogue with daily prayer services, weekly Torah classes, and youth groups on Shabbat. The site has a page for visitors who want to spend a Shabbos there.
records.what_you_do: Pray at Shabbat or weekday services, attend a Torah class, bring young children to Moms & Tots on Shabbos and Yom Tov mornings, or bring older children to the Shabbos morning groups. You can also sponsor a kiddush or Shalosh Seudos meal, or fill in the online membership form.

schedule.text: Shabbat morning services begin at 9 am, after a parsha class at 8:30 am. Moms & Tots runs every Shabbos and Yom Tov morning, and children's groups meet on select Shabbos mornings. Weekday morning minyanim are around 6:20 to 6:45 am, and Mincha and Maariv are in the evening. The site posted these times for a September week, so confirm before you go.

cost.text: Membership and donation options are listed on the site, but no amounts are printed.

first_step.how: Fill in the short Visit for a Shabbos form on the site, which asks for a name and email, or email info@biozshul.org to ask about visiting.
first_step.basis: The site has a Visit for a Shabbos form and an email address, and the contact page says the shul warmly welcomes inquiries. It does not describe what a first visit is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shabbos morning services start at 9 am after a parsha class at 8:30, and children have their own groups on select Shabbos mornings. The Visit for a Shabbos page does not describe hosting, meals, or sleeping, so ask the shul by email first.
first_visit_tips: Email info@biozshul.org with your questions before you come.
Check the posted times against the current schedule, since the site's times were printed for a September week.

records.notes: The last dated item is a shul-listed tour for October 13, 2026 (registration required) on the programming page; it is used only for last_sign_of_life. The contact page lists a second inquiry address and a personal number for emergencies only; neither is recorded. Moms & Tots ages are not stated. Membership payment is on a third-party domain, which is not recorded.

records.name: Congregation Leyv Ha-Ir (Heart of the City)
records.summary: A small Reconstructionist congregation that meets mostly at the Ethical Society building near Rittenhouse Square. Members take part in worship, holiday events, adult classes, social justice work, and the choir.
records.what_you_do: Join Friday services and holiday events, take part in adult education (mostly on Zoom), sing in the Kol Ha'Leyv choir, or join a social justice project. The congregation says it has affordable dues options.

schedule.text: Monthly Friday evening Kabbalat Shabbat with a community dinner before, a monthly Shabbat morning service, and a monthly Rosh Chodesh gathering for women. Shamanu Sessions meet online each week for members. Exact dates and times are on the event calendar.

cost.text: Suggested yearly dues are $650 to $1,200 for a single membership and $975 to $1,700 for a family membership. Membership includes access to all programs, and the site says no one is turned away for money reasons.

first_step.how: Email info@leyvhair.org or call 215.629.1995 to ask whether a guest can come to a Friday service before joining, or use the Click To Join form on the site.
first_step.basis: Events and a join form are listed publicly, but the site does not say whether guests may attend before joining, and membership is described as including access to programs.
first_step.what_to_expect: Friday services are monthly and include a community dinner before and a community social hour (oneg) after, led by the rabbi and one other spiritual leader. The site does not say how long a service runs, what to wear, or whether guests pay anything.
first_visit_tips: Ask the office whether a guest can come to a Friday service before you join.
Most programs also run on Zoom, so ask about joining online if that is easier.

records.notes: The events calendar page loaded no listings, so no dated events were found and status is unchanged. Choir rehearsal times and place are not on the site. The worship address is not on the site (only a P.O. box), so the Ethical Society building address carries over from tier 1. Discussion groups marked for members only are not open to visitors.

records.name: Congregation Mikveh Israel
records.summary: A historic congregation at 44 North Fourth Street. It offers weekday morning and afternoon prayer services with a free breakfast or lunch, Shabbat services, public tours, and a museum exhibit.
records.what_you_do: Join the weekday morning Shacharit or the afternoon Minha minyan, book the historic synagogue tour, see the Faith and Freedom exhibition, join the Thursday evening Zoom class, or sign a child up for the Monday after-school class.

schedule.text: Weekday Shacharit at 7:15 am on Mondays, Thursdays, and Rosh Chodesh, and Minha at 2 pm Monday to Thursday. Shabbat services are weekly, so check the site for the current Friday evening and Saturday morning times. Also weekly: a Thursday 7:30 pm Zoom class and a Monday 4 to 5 pm after-school class for children ages 5 to 12.

cost.text: Weekday breakfast or lunch with the minyanim is free, and parking is free with the weekday minyanim. Shabbat and holiday meals have prices, but the amounts are not printed on the site.

first_step.how: Come to the 7:15 am weekday minyan on a Monday or Thursday, where breakfast is free afterward, or call the office at 215-922-5446 to book a public tour.
first_step.basis: The Rabbis' Welcome page invites visitors to come in person to Shabbat, a daily minyan, or the exhibits, and the site lists how to book a tour and how to join the WhatsApp group for the minyan.
first_step.what_to_expect: Services follow the congregation's Spanish-Portuguese tradition, which the site describes as formal and orderly, with careful Hebrew pronunciation. Members often attend the morning service so there is a minyan for those saying Kaddish, and free breakfast or lunch follows the weekday minyanim. The site does not say how long services run or what to wear.
first_visit_tips: Call or email the office first, since it is open Monday to Thursday 9 am to 5 pm and Friday 9 am to 3 pm.
Parking is free with the weekday minyanim.
Arrive a few minutes before 7:15 am for the morning minyan.

records.notes: The self-guided museum tour page gives nine stops but no cost, hours, or length. Shabbat times on the site change weekly and are not recorded. The children's class started October 12, 2025 per the site; its teacher and cost are not stated. Shabbat and holiday meal prices are not printed.
